Theme

Latin word

difficilis

difficilis, difficile

adjective, third declension

hard to please, awkward; difficult, hard; difficult, hard to manage, contrary

In this lexicon

  • critical

    also used · classical · Cic. Or. 104 (Lewis & Short, s.v. mōrōsus)

  • difficult

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Heaut. 805–806; Catull. 76.13: difficile est longum subitō dēpōnere amōrem; Traupman 304

  • difficult

    the recommended word · classical · Mart. 12.46.1: difficilis facilis, jūcundus acerbus es īdem; Cic. Sen. 65: mōrōsī et anxiī et īrācundī et difficilēs senēs; Ter. Heaut. 535: hunc difficilem invītum servāret senem

Examples

  • Nūlla est tam facilis rēs quīn difficilis siet, quam invītus faciās.

    Nothing is so easy that it isn’t difficult when you do it against your will.Ter. Heaut. 805–806

    In the entry for difficult

  • Nihil tam difficile est quīn quaerendō investīgārī possiet.

    Nothing is so difficult that it can’t be tracked down by searching.Ter. Heaut. 675

    In the entry for difficult

  • nōn quia difficilia sunt nōn audēmus, sed quia nōn audēmus difficilia sunt

    it is not because things are difficult that we don’t dare; it is because we don’t dare that they are difficultSen. Ep. 104.26

    In the entry for difficult

  • Difficile factū est, sed cōnābor nihilō sētius.

    It’s hard to do, but I’ll try just the same.Traupman p. 100

    In the entry for difficult
